children.text: ghuṣyate yasya nagare raṅgayātrā dine dine /
children.translated_text: He in whose city the festival procession of <s>Raṅga</s> (<s>Raṅganātha</s>) is celebrated day after day —

children.text: tam ahaṃ śirasā vande rājānaṃ kulaśekharam //
children.translated_text: I bow my head to that king, <s>Kulaśekhara</s>.

children.text: śrīvallabheti varadeti dayāpareti bhaktapriyeti bhavaluṇṭhanakovideti /
children.translated_text: O Beloved of <s>Śrī</s>! O Bestower of Boons! O You who are Compassion itself! O You who are dear to Your devotees! O You who are skilled in destroying worldly existence!

children.text: nātheti nāgaśayaneti jagannivāsety ālāpinaṃ pratidinaṃ kuru māṃ mukunda || 1 ||
children.translated_text: O Lord! O You who recline upon the serpent (<s>Nāgaśayana</s>)! O Dwelling-place of the universe! — Make me one who calls upon [You] with [these names] every day, O <s>Mukunda</s>!

children.text: jayatu jayatu devo devakīnandano 'yaṃ jayatu jayatu kṛṣṇo vṛṣṇivaṃśapradīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Victory, victory to this god, the joy of <s>Devakī</s>! Victory, victory to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lamp of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> lineage!

children.text: jayatu jayatu meghaśyāmalaḥ komalāṅgo jayatu jayatu pṛthvībhāranāśo mukundaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: Victory, victory to Him who is cloud-dark with tender limbs! Victory, victory to <s>Mukunda</s>, the destroyer of the earth's burden!

children.text: mukunda mūrdhnā praṇipatya yāce bhavantam ekāntam iyantam artham /
children.translated_text: O <s>Mukunda</s>, bowing my head, I beseech You for this one exclusive and limited desire:

children.text: avismṛtis tvaccaraṇāravinde bhave bhave me 'stu bhavatprasādāt || 3 ||
children.translated_text: May there be unfailing remembrance of Your lotus-feet, in birth after birth, by Your grace!

children.text: nāhaṃ vande tava caraṇayor dvandvam advandvahetoḥ kumbhīpākaṃ gurum api hare nārakaṃ nāpanetum /
children.translated_text: I do not worship the pair of Your feet in order to be free from the pairs [of opposites], nor to be rescued from the terrible <s>Kumbhīpāka</s> (hell of boiling oil), O <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: ramyā rāmā mṛdutanulatā nandane nāpi rantuṃ bhāve bhāve hṛdayabhavane bhāvayeyaṃ bhavantam || 4 ||
children.translated_text: nor to sport with lovely women of tender vine-like bodies in <s>Nandana</s> (the heavenly garden) — [but rather] in birth after birth, in the temple of my heart, may I contemplate You!

children.text: nāsthā dharme na vasunicaye naiva kāmopabhoge yad bhāvyaṃ tad bhavatu bhagavan pūrvakarmānurūpam /
children.translated_text: I have no interest in <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), nor in accumulation of wealth, nor in enjoyment of desires — let whatever is destined come to pass, O Blessed Lord, in accordance with prior <s>karma</s>;

children.text: etat prārthyaṃ mama bahu-mataṃ janmajanmāntare 'pi tvatpādāmbhoruhayugagatā niścalā bhaktir astu || 5 ||
children.translated_text: this alone is my highest prayer, birth after birth: may there be unwavering <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) directed to the pair of Your lotus-feet!

children.text: divi vā bhuvi vā mamāstu vāso narake vā narakāntaka prakāmam /
children.translated_text: Whether my dwelling be in heaven or on earth, or even in hell — O Destroyer of Hell, [let it be] freely!

children.text: avadhīritaśāradāravindau caraṇau te maraṇe 'pi cintayāmi || 6 ||
children.translated_text: Your feet, which put to shame the autumnal lotuses — even in death, I shall contemplate them.

children.text: kṛṣṇa tvadīyapadapaṅkajapañjarāntar adyaiva me viśatu mānasarājahaṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, let the royal swan of my mind enter today itself into the cage of Your lotus-feet;

children.text: prāṇaprayāṇasamaye kaphavātapittaiḥ kaṇṭhāvarodhanavidhau smaraṇaṃ kutas te || 7 ||
children.translated_text: at the time of the departure of the vital breath, when the throat is obstructed by phlegm, wind, and bile — how can there be remembrance of You then?

children.text: cintayāmi harim eva santataṃ mandamandahāsitānanāmbujam /
children.translated_text: I contemplate <s>Hari</s> alone constantly, His lotus-face gently, gently smiling,

children.text: nandagopatanayaṃ parāt paraṃ nāradādimunivṛndavanditam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Nandagopa</s>, the highest beyond the highest, worshiped by hosts of sages beginning with <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: karacaraṇasaroje kāntimannetramīne śramamuṣi bhujavīcivyākule 'gādhamārge /
children.translated_text: In the lake of <s>Hari</s> — where the lotus-hands and feet are the lotuses, the radiant eyes are the fish, [the lake is] fatigue-dispelling, the waves of the arms cause tumult, and the depth is unfathomable —

children.text: harisarasi vigāhyāpīya tejojalaughaṃ bhavamaruparikhinnaḥ khedam adya tyajāmi || 9 ||
children.translated_text: having plunged in and drunk deep of the flood of luminous waters, I, exhausted by the desert of worldly existence, today cast off my weariness.

children.text: sarasijanayane saśaṅkhacakre murabhidi mā viramasva citta rantum /
children.translated_text: O mind, do not cease to delight in the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, who has lotus-eyes and bears the conch and discus;

children.text: sukhataram aparaṃ na jātu jāne haricaraṇasmaraṇāmṛtena tulyam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: I know nothing else more blissful than the nectar of remembering the feet of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: mābhīr mandamano vicintya bahudhā yāmīś ciraṃ yātanā nāmī naḥ prabhavanti pāparipavaḥ svāmī nanu śrīdharaḥ /
children.translated_text: Fear not, O sluggish mind, thinking at length of the punishments of <s>Yama</s> [endured] for a long time! These sinful enemies cannot prevail over us — for our Lord is none other than <s>Śrīdhara</s> (the bearer of <s>Śrī</s>)!

children.text: ālasyaṃ vyapanīya bhaktisulabhaṃ dhyāyasva nārāyaṇaṃ lokasya vyasanāpanodanakaro dāsasya kiṃ na kṣamaḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: Casting aside sloth, meditate upon <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who is easily attainable through <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) — He who removes the afflictions of the world, is He not capable [of doing so] for His servant?

children.text: bhavajaladhigatānāṃ dvandvavātāhatānāṃ sutaduhitṛkalatratrāṇabhārārditānām /
children.translated_text: For those who have entered the ocean of worldly existence, battered by the winds of dualities, afflicted by the burden of protecting sons, daughters, and wives,

children.text: viṣamaviṣayatoye majjatām aplavānāṃ bhavatu śaraṇam eko viṣṇupoto narāṇām || 12 ||
children.translated_text: drowning in the treacherous waters of sense-objects without a raft — may the ship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone be the refuge of men!

children.text: bhavajaladhim agādhaṃ dustaraṃ nistareyaṃ katham aham iti ceto mā sma gāḥ kātaratvam /
children.translated_text: 'How shall I cross this fathomless, impassable ocean of worldly existence?' — O mind, do not give way to such cowardice!

children.text: sarasijadṛśi deve tāvakī bhaktir ekā narakabhidi niṣaṇṇā tārayiṣyaty avaśyam || 13 ||
children.translated_text: Your singular <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to the lotus-eyed God, firmly seated in the Destroyer of Hell, shall certainly ferry [you] across!

children.text: tṛṣṇātoye madanapavanoddhūtamohormimāle dārāvarte tanayasahajagrāhasaṅghākule ca /
children.translated_text: In the great ocean called <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth), with the waters of craving, the waves of delusion stirred up by the wind of passion, the whirlpools of wife, and teeming with the crocodiles that are sons and companions —

children.text: saṃsārākhye mahati jaladhau majjatāṃ nas tridhāman pādāmbhoje varada bhavato bhaktināvaṃ prayaccha || 14 ||
children.translated_text: for us who are drowning, O <s>Tridhāman</s> (Lord of the three abodes), O Bestower of boons, grant the boat of devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to Your lotus-feet!

children.text: mā drākṣaṃ kṣīṇapuṇyān kṣaṇam api bhavato bhaktihīnān padābje mā śrauṣaṃ śrāvyabandhaṃ tava caritam apāsyānyad ākhyānajātam /
children.translated_text: May I never behold, even for a moment, those of exhausted merit who are devoid of <s>bhakti</s> to Your lotus-feet! May I never hear any collection of tales other than the account of Your deeds, which are worthy of hearing!

children.text: mā smārṣaṃ mādhava tvām api bhuvanapate cetasāpahnuvānān mā bhūvaṃ tvatsaparyāvyatikararahito janmajanmāntare 'pi || 15 ||
children.translated_text: May I never remember, O <s>Mādhava</s>, those who deny You, the Lord of the universe, even in their minds! May I never be deprived of Your worship, birth after birth!

children.text: jihve kīrtaya keśavaṃ muraripuṃ ceto bhaja śrīdharaṃ pāṇidvandva samarcayācyutakathāḥ śrotradvaya tvaṃ śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: O tongue, glorify <s>Keśava</s>, the enemy of <s>Mura</s>! O mind, worship <s>Śrīdhara</s>! O pair of hands, adore [Him]! O pair of ears, listen to the stories of <s>Acyuta</s>!

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ lokaya locanadvaya harer gacchāṅghriyugmālayaṃ jighra ghrāṇa mukundapādatulasīṃ mūrdhan namādhokṣajam || 16 ||
children.translated_text: O pair of eyes, behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O pair of feet, go to the temple of <s>Hari</s>! O nose, smell the <s>tulasī</s> (holy basil) from <s>Mukunda</s>'s feet! O head, bow to <s>Adhokṣaja</s>!

children.text: he lokāḥ śṛṇuta prasūtimaraṇavyādheś cikitsām imāṃ yogajñāḥ samudāharanti munayo yāṃ yājñavalkyādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: O people! Hear this remedy for the disease of birth and death, which the sages versed in yoga, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> and others, prescribe:

children.text: antarjyotir ameyam ekam amṛtaṃ kṛṣṇākhyam āpīyatāṃ tat pītaṃ paramauṣadhaṃ vitanute nirvāṇam ātyantikam || 17 ||
children.translated_text: let the inner light — immeasurable, singular, immortal, called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — be drunk! That supreme medicine, once drunk, bestows ultimate <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // 17 //

children.text: he martyāḥ paramaṃ hitaṃ śṛṇuta vo vakṣyāmi saṅkṣepataḥ saṃsārārṇavam āpadūrmibahulaṃ samyak praviśya sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: O mortals! Hear the supreme benefit — I shall tell you briefly. You who have well entered and are standing in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, teeming with waves of calamity —

children.text: nānājñānam apāsya cetasi namo nārāyaṇāyety amuṃ mantraṃ sapraṇavaṃ praṇāmasahitaṃ prāvartayadhvaṃ muhuḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: casting aside all other knowledge, set in motion in your hearts this <s>mantra</s>: 'Namo Nārāyaṇāya,' with the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and accompanied by obeisance, again and again! // 18 //

children.text: pṛthvī reṇur aṇuḥ payāṃsi kaṇikāḥ phalguḥ sphuliṅgo laghuḥ tejo niḥśvasanaṃ marut tanutaraṃ randhraṃ susūkṣmaṃ nabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Earth is [but] a speck of dust, an atom; the waters are [but] droplets; fire is a trifling spark; wind is [but] a faint breath; space is a very subtle hole —

children.text: kṣudrā rudrapitāmahaprabhṛtayaḥ kīṭāḥ samastāḥ surāḥ dṛṣṭe yatra sa tāvako vijayate bhūmāvadhūtāvadhiḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: insignificant are <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s> (Brahmā), and the rest; all the gods are [mere] insects — when He is seen, that Lord of Yours triumphs, whose greatness defies all measure. // 19 //

children.text: baddhenāñjalinā natena śirasā gātraiḥ saromodgamaiḥ kaṇṭhena svaragadgadena nayanenodgīrṇabāṣpāmbunā /
children.translated_text: With palms joined together, with head bowed low, with limbs bristling with goosebumps, with voice choked in the throat, with eyes shedding forth a flood of tears —

children.text: nityaṃ tvaccaraṇāravindayugaladhyānāmṛtāsvādinām asmākaṃ sarasīruhākṣa satataṃ sampadyatāṃ jīvitam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: may our life be always [spent] savoring the nectar of meditation on the pair of Your lotus-feet, O lotus-eyed one! // 20 //

children.text: he gopālaka he kṛpājalanidhe he sindhukanyāpate he kaṃsāntaka he gajendrakaruṇāpārīṇa he mādhava /
children.translated_text: O Cowherd! O ocean of compassion! O Lord of the daughter of the ocean! O slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>! O You who showed limitless compassion to the king of elephants! O <s>Mādhava</s>!

children.text: he rāmānuja he jagattrayaguro he puṇḍarīkākṣa māṃ he gopījananātha pālaya paraṃ jānāmi na tvāṃ vinā || 21 ||
children.translated_text: O younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>! O Teacher of the three worlds! O lotus-eyed one! O Lord of the <s>gopī</s> women — protect me! I know no one other than You. // 21 //

children.text: bhaktāpāyabhujāṅgagāruḍamaṇis trailokyarakṣāmaṇir gopīlocanacātakāmbudamaṇiḥ saundaryamudrāmaṇiḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Garuḍa</s>-gem against the serpent of devotees' misfortune, the protective jewel of the three worlds, the rain-cloud gem for the <s>cātaka</s>-birds that are the <s>gopīs</s>' eyes, the seal-gem of beauty,

children.text: yaḥ kāntāmaṇirukmiṇīghanakucadvandvaikabhūṣāmaṇiḥ śreyo devaśikhāmaṇir diśatu no gopālacūḍāmaṇiḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: He who is the beloved gem, the sole ornamental jewel for the pair of ample breasts of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> — may the crest-jewel of the gods, the crown-jewel of the cowherds, bestow good fortune upon us. // 22 //

children.text: śatrucchedaikamantraṃ sakalam upaniṣadvākyasampūjyamantraṃ saṃsārottāramantraṃ samupacitatamasaḥ saṅghaniryāṇamantram /
children.translated_text: The one <s>mantra</s> for destroying enemies, the <s>mantra</s> supremely honored by all <s>Upaniṣad</s> utterances, the <s>mantra</s> for crossing over <s>saṃsāra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> for the departure of the accumulated mass of darkness,

children.text: sarvaiśvaryaikamantraṃ vyasanabhujagasandaṣṭasantrāṇamantraṃ jihve śrīkṛṣṇamantraṃ japa japa satataṃ janmasāphalyamantram || 23 ||
children.translated_text: the one <s>mantra</s> for all sovereignty, the <s>mantra</s> for rescuing one bitten by the serpent of adversity — O tongue, chant, chant constantly the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa mantra</s>, the <s>mantra</s> that makes birth fruitful! // 23 //

children.text: vyāmohapraśamauṣadhaṃ munimanovṛttipravṛttyauṣadhaṃ daityendrārtikarauṣadhaṃ tribhuvane sañjīvanaikauṣadham /
children.translated_text: The medicine for quelling delusion, the medicine that sets in motion the mental activity of sages, the medicine that causes affliction to the lord of demons, the sole life-restoring medicine in the three worlds,

children.text: bhaktātyantahitauṣadhaṃ bhavabhayapradhvaṃsanaikauṣadhaṃ śreyaḥprāptikarauṣadhaṃ piba manaḥ śrīkṛṣṇadivyauṣadham || 24 ||
children.translated_text: the medicine supremely beneficial to devotees, the sole medicine for destroying the fear of worldly existence, the medicine that brings about the attainment of the highest good — O mind, drink the divine medicine of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>! // 24 //

children.text: āmnāyābhyasanāny araṇyaruditaṃ vedavratāny anvahaṃ medaśchedaphalāni pūrtavidhayaḥ sarve hutaṃ bhasmani /
children.translated_text: The study of the sacred texts, weeping in the forest, the daily observances of the <s>Vedas</s>, austerities whose fruit is the cutting of fat, the rites of charitable works — all are [like] an offering poured into ashes,

children.text: tīrthānām avagāhanāni ca gajasnānaṃ vinā yatpada-dvandvāmbhoruhasaṃsmṛtīr vijayate devaḥ sa nārāyaṇaḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: [all are like] an elephant's bath at sacred fords — without the remembrance of that pair of lotus-feet! Victorious is that God, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>! // 25 //

children.text: śrīmannāma procya nārāyaṇākhyaṃ ke na prāpur vāñchitaṃ pāpino 'pi /
children.translated_text: Having uttered the auspicious name called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who has not attained their desires — even sinners?

children.text: hā naḥ pūrvaṃ vāk pravṛttā na tasmiṃs tena prāptaṃ garbhavāsādiduḥkham || 26 ||
children.translated_text: Alas, our speech was not previously directed toward Him; because of that, the suffering of dwelling in the womb and the like was obtained! // 26 //

children.text: majjanmanaḥ phalam idaṃ madhukaiṭabhāre matprārthanīyamadanugraha eṣa eva /
children.translated_text: This is the fruit of my birth, O enemy of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>; this alone is the favor I seek from You:

children.text: tvadbhṛtyabhṛtyaparicārakabhṛtyabhṛtya-bhṛtyasya bhṛtya iti māṃ smara lokanātha || 27 ||
children.translated_text: 'A servant of the servant of the attendant of the servant of the servant of the servant of Your servant' — remember me thus, O Lord of the world! // 27 //

children.text: nāthe naḥ puruṣottame trijagatāṃ ekādhipe cetasā sevye svasya padasya dātari sure nārāyaṇe tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: While <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, our Lord, the Supreme Person, the sole sovereign of the three worlds, worthy of being served with the heart, the God who grants His own abode, stands [ready] —

children.text: yaṃ kañcit puruṣādhamaṃ katipayagrāmeśam alpārthadaṃ sevāyai mṛgayāmahe naram aho mūkā varākā vayam || 28 ||
children.translated_text: that we seek out some lowly man, a petty lord of a few villages, who gives trifling things, for service — alas, we are mute and wretched! // 28 //

children.text: madana parihara sthitiṃ madīye manasi mukundapadāravindadhāmni /
children.translated_text: O <s>Madana</s> (god of love), abandon your position in my mind, which is the abode of the lotus-feet of <s>Mukunda</s>!

children.text: haranayanakṛśānunā kṛśo 'si smarasi na cakraparākramaṃ murāreḥ || 29 ||
children.translated_text: You were reduced to ashes by the fire of <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) eye — do you not remember the might of the discus of <s>Murāri</s>? // 29 //

children.text: tattvaṃ bruvāṇāni paraṃ parastān madhu kṣarantīva satāṃ phalāni /
children.translated_text: Speaking the ultimate truth beyond all truths, as though dripping honey — the fruits that benefit the virtuous —

children.text: prāvartaya prāñjalir asmi jihve nāmāni nārāyaṇagocarāṇi || 30 ||
children.translated_text: O tongue, set them forth! I stand with palms joined — the names that pertain to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>! // 30 //

children.text: idaṃ śarīraṃ pariṇāmapeśalaṃ pataty avaśyaṃ ślathasandhijarjaram /
children.translated_text: This body, beautiful only in its [constant] transformation, will inevitably fall, decrepit with loosened joints.

children.text: kim auṣadhaiḥ kliśyasi mūḍha durmate nirāmayaṃ kṛṣṇarasāyanaṃ piba || 31 ||
children.translated_text: Why do you torment yourself with medicines, O foolish, deluded one? Drink the disease-free elixir of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! // 31 //

children.text: dārā vārākaravarasutā te tanūjo viriñcaḥ stotā vedas tava suragaṇo bhṛtyavargaḥ prasādaḥ /
children.translated_text: Your wife is the excellent daughter of the ocean (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); Your son is <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>); Your praiser is the <s>Veda</s>; the host of gods is Your retinue of servants; [Your] grace —

children.text: muktir māyā jagad avikalaṃ tāvakī devakī te mātā mitraṃ balaripusutas tvayy ato 'nyan na jāne || 32 ||
children.translated_text: liberation is Your <s>Māyā</s>; the entire world is Yours; <s>Devakī</s> is Your mother; Your friend is the son of the enemy of <s>Bala</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>, son of <s>Indra</s>) — beyond You I know nothing else. (32)

children.text: kṛṣṇo rakṣatu no jagattrayaguruḥ kṛṣṇaṃ namasyāmy ahaṃ kṛṣṇenāmaraśatravo vinihatāḥ kṛṣṇāya tasmai namaḥ /
children.translated_text: May <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>guru</s> of the three worlds, protect us! I bow to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! By <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the enemies of the gods were slain — to that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, salutations!

children.text: kṛṣṇād eva samutthitaṃ jagad idaṃ kṛṣṇasya dāso 'smy ahaṃ kṛṣṇe tiṣṭhati sarvam etad akhilaṃ he kṛṣṇa saṃrakṣa mām || 33 ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone this world has arisen; I am the servant of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> rests all of this entirely — O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, protect me! (33)

children.text: sa tvaṃ prasīda bhagavan kuru mayy anāthe viṣṇo kṛpāṃ paramakāruṇikaḥ kila tvam /
children.translated_text: Be pleased, O Lord! Show mercy to me, the destitute one, O <s>Viṣṇu</s> — for You are supremely compassionate!

children.text: saṃsārasāgaranimagnam ananta dīnam uddhartum arhasi hare puruṣottamo 'si || 34 ||
children.translated_text: Sunk in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, wretched, O <s>Ananta</s> (Infinite One) — You are worthy to lift [me] up, O <s>Hari</s>, for You are the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>)! (34)

children.text: namāmi nārāyaṇapādapaṅkajaṃ karomi nārāyaṇapūjanaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: I bow to the lotus-feet of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; I always perform worship of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: vadāmi nārāyaṇanāma nirmalaṃ smarāmi nārāyaṇatattvam avyayam || 35 ||
children.translated_text: I speak the pure name of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; I remember the imperishable truth (<s>tattva</s>) of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. (35)

children.text: śrīnātha nārāyaṇa vāsudeva śrīkṛṣṇa bhaktapriya cakrapāṇe /
children.translated_text: O Lord of <s>Śrī</s>! O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>! O <s>Vāsudeva</s>! O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, dear to devotees, O wielder of the discus (<s>Cakrapāṇi</s>)!

children.text: śrīpadmanābhācyuta kaiṭabhāre śrīrāma padmākṣa hare murāre || 36 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrī Padmanābha</s>! O <s>Acyuta</s> (Infallible One)! O slayer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s>! O <s>Śrī Rāma</s>! O lotus-eyed (<s>Padmākṣa</s>)! O <s>Hari</s>! O <s>Murāri</s> (slayer of <s>Mura</s>)! (36)

children.text: ananta vaikuṇṭha mukunda kṛṣṇa govinda dāmodara mādhaveti /
children.translated_text: O <s>Ananta</s>! O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>! O <s>Mukunda</s>! O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Govinda</s>! O <s>Dāmodara</s>! O <s>Mādhava</s>! —

children.text: vaktuṃ samartho 'pi na vakti kaścid aho janānāṃ vyasanābhimukhyam || 37 ||
children.translated_text: though capable of uttering [these names], no one utters them. Alas, the predilection of people for misfortune! (37)

children.text: dhyāyanti ye viṣṇum anantam avyayaṃ hṛtpadmamadhye satataṃ vyavasthitam /
children.translated_text: Those who meditate on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the infinite and imperishable, forever established in the lotus of the heart,

children.text: samāhitānāṃ satatābhaya-pradaṃ te yānti siddhiṃ paramāṃ tu vaiṣṇavīm || 38 ||
children.translated_text: who is the constant bestower of fearlessness to the concentrated — they attain the supreme <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> perfection (<s>siddhi</s>). (38)

children.text: kṣīrasāgarataraṅgaśīkarā-sāratārakitacārumūrtaye /
children.translated_text: To Him whose beautiful form is spangled like stars by the sprinkled essence of the waves of the milk-ocean,

children.text: bhogibhogaśayanīyaśāyine mādhavāya madhuvidviṣe namaḥ || 39 ||
children.translated_text: who reclines upon the couch that is the coils of the serpent [<s>Śeṣa</s>] — to <s>Mādhava</s>, the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, salutations! (39)

children.text: yasya priyau śrutidharau kavilokavīrau mitre dvijanmavarapadmaśarāv abhūtām /
children.translated_text: He whose two dear ones, upholders of the <s>Śruti</s>, heroes of the world of poets, were the excellent twice-born friends <s>Padma</s> and <s>Śara</s> —

children.text: tenāmbujākṣacaraṇāmbujaṣaṭpadena rājñā kṛtā kṛtir iyaṃ kulaśekhareṇa || 40 ||
children.translated_text: by him, a bee at the lotus-feet of the lotus-eyed Lord, by the king <s>Kulaśekhara</s>, this composition was made. (40)
